subject: Yakaboylu, "Hamiltonian for the Hilbert-Pólya Conjecture", arXiv:2309.00405 (v6), J. Phys. A 57 (2024) 235204
claim: The claimed existence of a similarity transformation making the Hamiltonian self-adjoint on a domain fixed by a zeta-zero boundary condition fails: the weight (18) defines an indefinite form (explicit vector with <U|U> = -0.0231), and the boundary condition (17) admits spurious solutions where zeta(s) != 0 (e.g. s = 1/2 + 3.70362i). The paper itself states its argument is formal and does not claim a proof of RH.
witness: Explicit numerical witnesses; independent two-sided adjudication

subject: Farmer, "Jensen polynomials are not a plausible route to proving the Riemann Hypothesis", Adv. Math. 411 (2022) 108781; arXiv:2008.07206
location: Sec. 4.2, Table 4.1 and the sentence on X_10
claim: Table 4.1 thresholds do not match the configuration described in the text (printed j=20 threshold corresponds to moving 9pi/2, 11pi/2, not the two zeros closest to 20, whose threshold is 478; j=10: certified 120 vs printed 119). The paper's qualitative conclusion is not affected.
witness: Arb-certified exact Jensen-polynomial root counts (campaign C1) independently recomputed by the L2 auditor and adjudicator

subject: Bellotti-Trudgian-Yang, "Zero-free regions inspired by work of Heath-Brown", arXiv:2603.21490v1 (2026 preprint)
claim: m_5 = 0.00735709 is not a lower bound for min_x G_5(1,x) with the paper's stated rational polynomial (certified minimum in (0.0073564918, 0.0073564919)); entries appear computed from Mossinghoff-Trudgian's floating-point F16. With the corrected entry sum (log p) m_p = 0.2354513 > 0.23545, so Theorem 1 and the constant 4.896 are unaffected. The Observatory independently reproduced the 4.896 chain (eta log t > 0.2042602). Separately, Lemma 4's constant c0 is mis-transcribed from Ford (typo; later numbers use the correct value).
witness: Arb ball evaluations, exact rational evaluation, root isolation; independent adjudication. Allowed public wording: a localized table entry invalid for the stated polynomial, with a corrected value preserving the theorem. Never an error in the 4.896 region.

subject: Alpöge-Furman, "More than two thirds of the zeta zeros are simple and on the critical line", arXiv:2608.13637v2 (2026 preprint)
location: proof of Prop. 4.2 (LaTeX l.327, PDF p.6)
claim: The proof applies a distance bound |Re gamma_rho - alpha_k| >= D_rho to zeros with Re gamma_rho in I'\I, where it is false (explicit witnesses on actual zeta zeros). A short repair using one-sided decay (the estimate the authors use in Props 4.3 and 5.2) restores tr G = N(I') + O(sqrt T log T), within the stated error; Prop. 4.2, the Section 6 chain and Theorems A and B are unaffected.
witness: Numerical witnesses at T up to 3e4 with two cut-offs; independent adjudication

subject: A. Yang, "Explicit bounds on zeta(s) in the critical strip and a zero-free region", arXiv:2301.03165 v1/v2; JMAA 534 (2024)
claim: The constant change between versions is a version difference, and downstream constants (Bellotti 2024, BTY 2026, Fiori-Jaskari 2026) are not weakened. The auditor reports that the written argument does not cover v1's 21.432 for the full stated range; adjudication kept this as a suspected gap without a public witness.
witness: Crossover recomputations; not a verified witness

subject: Connes, "Trace formula in noncommutative geometry and the zeros of the Riemann zeta function", Selecta Math. 5 (1999); arXiv:math/9811068
claim: Theorem 5 (equivalence of the global trace formula with RH for Hecke L-functions) is proved for global fields of positive characteristic; for number fields the paper reduces RH to a trace-formula/positivity statement that is not proved. Citations attributing a proved number-field result misread the paper.
witness: Text of Sec. VIII; citation survey

subject: Andrade-Keating, "Conjectures for the integral moments and ratios of L-functions over function fields", J. Number Theory 142 (2014); arXiv:1407.3099
claim: Theorem 1 and Sec. 5.3 rest on Conjecture 5; later citations should carry the conditionality.

subject: Ng-Shen-Wong, "The eighth moment of the Riemann zeta function", J. Eur. Math. Soc. 28 (2026); arXiv:2204.13891
location: Prop. 3.1 / import of Thm 1.2 of "Shifted moments"
classification: correct_but_misinterpreted (by the Observatory reader); minor citation-range mismatch
claim: All hypotheses of the imported theorem hold where used (k = 4). The Observatory Level-1 reader's "k >= 12" was a pdftotext artifact (\frac{1}{2} rendered as "12"). Minor: the paper quotes the imported range as k >= 1/2 whereas the companion proves k >= 1; immaterial at k = 4. Theorem 1.1 is conditional on RH and a quaternary additive divisor conjecture.

subject: OpenAI, "The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis" (11/12 companion), 5 Oct 2026; github.com/openai/math@4eaee875, paper2.pdf sha256 f919b578...
claim: Section-by-section Level-2 audit by seven auditor agents found no mathematical error; about one hundred numerical checks of the arithmetic identities (sextic/cubic residue symbols, Gauss sums, reciprocity, Gauss-Jacobi relations, cubic-theta transformation data) were confirmed in Z[omega]. Only presentational issues were found. Imported inputs (Patterson/Kubota cubic theta, Dunn-Radziwill cusp expansions, large-sieve inputs) were checked against their statements but not re-proved. This is not a refereeing verdict.

subject: Conrey-Li (IMRN 2000) de Branges necessary zero condition
claim: The necessary condition -Re{xi'(rho_n) xi(1+rho_n)} >= 0 fails frequently, not only at Conrey-Li's witness: 195/2000, 2724/20000 and 15567/100000 zeros (three independent Arb implementations), with failure rates in 1000-zero blocks rising from 8% to 22.4% up to n = 1e10. New exact identity (campaign C3 adjudication): the condition at the n-th zero holds iff S(gamma_n) - delta_n lies outside (3/4, 7/4) mod 2, with delta_n a bounded phase term.
witness: Arb counts; identity proof in C3 FINAL
